record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Does the Caccetta-Haggkvist conjecture hold for multipartite tournaments, meaning orientations of complete multipartite graphs: does every such digraph with n vertices and minimum out-degree k contain a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/k)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Does Conjecture 3.1 hold for multipartite tournaments?
An orientation of a complete multipartite graph is called a multipartite tournament.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A multipartite tournament is an orientation of a complete multipartite graph; equivalently, it is a digraph whose vertex set can be partitioned into independent sets ("parts") such that between any two vertices in different parts there is exactly one arc, and there are no arcs within a part. For a digraph D and a vertex v, the out-degree of v is the number of arcs leaving v, and the minimum out-degree of D is the minimum of these values over all vertices. The girth of D is the length of a shortest directed cycle in D (or infinity if D is acyclic).

Question: Does every multipartite tournament D on n vertices with minimum out-degree at least k contain a directed cycle of length at most ⌈n/k⌉? Equivalently, prove or disprove that the Caccetta–Häggkvist bound holds in this class: every orientation of a complete multipartite graph on n vertices with minimum out-degree k has girth at most ⌈n/k⌉.
artifact.status_search_result: The general Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture is well known to be open, with even the k = n/3 (triangle) case unresolved. Partial results exist for special classes (bipartite tournaments, digraphs with small independence number, forbidden subgraph variants), but no proof or disproof of the conjecture restricted to multipartite tournaments appears in the literature; the restricted statement is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Caccetta-Haggkvist Conjecture (West)
status_evidence.snippet: The Caccetta-Häggkvist Conjecture asserts that every oriented graph on n vertices without directed cycles of length at most l has minimum outdegree at most (n-1)/l. Even for l = 3 the conjecture is still open.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture, including the l=3 case, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture – Egres Open
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem page listing partial results and special cases of the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture and its natural restrictions are listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture for digraphs with small independence number
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the conjecture for digraphs with small independence number, indicating the general and multipartite cases remain unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Only restricted cases have been settled; multipartite tournament case not established.
